profile.reading:
Per CoreSite's own facility page, this building, SV4, is located at 2972 Stender Way, Santa Clara, CA 95054, part of CoreSite's nine-building Silicon Valley campus. CoreSite publishes more than 101,000 square feet for this building. No MW capacity or opening year is stated. CoreSite lists SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA compliance for its facilities generally.

CoreSite's Santa Clara sub-campus (SV3 through SV9) is described in a CoreSite construction-approval release as exceeding 775,000 square feet combined, part of a nine-building, 1.4-million-plus-square-foot Silicon Valley presence spanning San Jose, Santa Clara, and Milpitas. CoreSite is a subsidiary of American Tower Corporation (NYSE: AMT), which completed its acquisition of CoreSite in late 2021; Stonepeak Partners LP separately acquired roughly 29% of American Tower's US data center business in July 2022, later increased to about 36%. CoreSite's own site describes a total portfolio of 30 data centers across 11 US markets totaling more than 4.8 million square feet, with more than 44,000 customer interconnections and 500-plus connected network providers.

American Tower reported record leasing at CoreSite driving stronger-than-expected second-quarter 2026 results, projecting data-center segment revenue of $1.20 billion to $1.22 billion for full-year 2026, roughly 14.9% growth at the midpoint, and raising its full-year outlook on the strength of that performance; the company also budgeted approximately $695 million in data-center development spending for 2026, funding continued build-out across CoreSite's 11-market US portfolio, of which the Santa Clara campus is among the largest by building count.

Stender Way, where SV4 sits, has become one of the more heavily built-up streets on CoreSite's Santa Clara campus, also hosting SV5, SV8, and SV9 within a few blocks, illustrating how colocation operators cluster multiple buildings tightly together to share fiber conduit, substations, and cooling infrastructure rather than spreading capacity across a wider footprint.

Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 34 (CoreSite missing-address campaign): added an operator-confirmed address and square footage, no MW figure available. research_status remains complete.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CoreSite was founded in 2001 as CRG West, a Carlyle Group portfolio company, beginning operations at two West Coast carrier hotel buildings, Market Post Tower and One Wilshire, both in Los Angeles. The firm rebranded from CRG West to CoreSite in June 2009 and completed an IPO in September 2010. American Tower Corporation, the public tower and infrastructure company (NYSE: AMT, SEC CIK 1053507), completed its acquisition of CoreSite in December 2021. Stonepeak Partners LP later bought roughly 29 percent of American Towers US data center business directly in July 2022, increasing that stake to about 36 percent by October 2022. CoreSites own current Silicon Valley regional page (operator source, tier-1, https://www.coresite.com/data-center-locations/silicon-valley) names nine data centers on this Santa Clara campus, SV1 through SV9, totaling more than 1.4 million square feet campus wide, but only describes SV1, SV2, SV4, SV7, SV8, and SV9 individually, SV1 and SV2 are not rows in this registry. SV3, SV5, and SV6 are not detailed on that page, so their building specific facts below come from data center industry aggregator directories instead. CoreSites own regional page gives this specific building, SV4, an address of 2972 Stender Way, Santa Clara, CA 95054, with 101,000 plus square feet, this is corroborated by industry aggregators Baxtel and DataCenterMap, which independently list the same address, and by a CoreSite branded spec sheet PDF hosted on the operators own web asset domain. No MW or power capacity figure was found for this specific building in any source checked this session.

reading.body:
CoreSite SV4 is a 101,000-square-foot building at 2972 Stender Way in Santa Clara, part of a nine-building Silicon Valley campus that spans more than 1.4 million square feet across San Jose, Santa Clara, and Milpitas. The operator publishes no megawatt capacity or power specification for this building. Without a stated IT load, translation to rack or accelerator count is not possible.

The building holds SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA certifications, meaning it qualifies to host regulated workloads in finance, healthcare, and government sectors. CoreSite, now owned by American Tower Corporation with Stonepeak Partners holding a 36 percent stake in the US data center portfolio, reported record leasing at CoreSite in 2026 and budgeted $695 million for data center development that year, of which the Santa Clara campus is among the largest by building count.

SV4 sits on Stender Way alongside three other CoreSite buildings, SV5, SV8, and SV9 within several blocks, a clustering pattern that concentrates fiber, substations, and cooling infrastructure to serve multiple buildings as a group rather than as dispersed sites. California has 103 mapped data center facilities; 11 publish power capacity totaling 365 MW. CoreSite's published capacity across the state ranks 12th, but this specific building contributes no disclosed figure to that ranking.
